content: Co-administration of medications that cause fluid and electrolyte abnormalities with magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride may increase the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Specific interactions include: 1. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and etodolac: This combination increases the toxicity of etodolac. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and fenoprofen: This combination increases the toxicity of fenoprofen. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferric carboxymaltose: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases the levels of ferric carboxymaltose by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 4. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferric citrate: This combination increases the toxicity of ferric citrate and decreases its levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. 5. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferric derisomaltose: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases the levels of ferric derisomaltose by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. 6. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferric gluconate: This combination decreases the levels of ferric gluconate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. 7. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferric maltol: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases the levels of ferric maltol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. 8. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferric pyrophosphate dialysate: This combination decreases the levels of ferric pyrophosphate dialysate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. 9. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferric pyrophosphate IV: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases the levels of ferric pyrophosphate IV by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. 10. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferrous fumarate: This combination decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. 11. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferrous gluconate: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases the levels of ferrous gluconate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. 12. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferrous sulfate: This combination decreases the levels of ferrous sulfate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. 13. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and ferumoxytol: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases the levels of ferumoxytol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer iron products at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose. 14. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and fludrocortisone: This combination increases the toxicity of fludrocortisone. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and fluoxetine: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the effects of fluoxetine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for evidence of seizures when using bowel preparations together with drugs that lower the seizure threshold. 16. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and fluphenazine: This combination increases the effects of fluphenazine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for enhanced central nervous system (CNS) depression when using higher doses of magnesium sulfate with a CNS depressant. 17. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and flurbiprofen: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of flurbiprofen. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and fluvoxamine: This combination increases the effects of fluvoxamine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for evidence of seizures when using bowel preparations together with drugs that lower the seizure threshold. 19. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and foscarnet: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of foscarnet. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and fosinopril: This combination increases the toxicity of fosinopril. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and gabapentin: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases the levels of gabapentin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer gabapentin at least 2 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 24. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and gemifloxacin: This combination decreases the levels of gemifloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 25. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and gentamicin: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of gentamicin. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and glasdegib: This combination increases the toxicity of glasdegib via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 27. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and haloperidol: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the effects of haloperidol by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for enhanced CNS depression when using higher doses of magnesium sulfate with a CNS depressant. 28. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 36.
